title: Module 5 · Anticoagulation
intro: DOAC dosing rules and catches, extended VTE therapy, warfarin interactions and reversal, DOAC reversal, heparin dosing, HIT, enoxaparin in kidney failure, procedures and bridging, duplicates and a night shift simulation.

cases.title: The apixaban 2 of 3 rule
cases.stem: An 82 year old woman, 64 kg, SCr 1.2 mg/dL, new atrial fibrillation. Order: apixaban 2.5 mg BID "because she is elderly."

steps.q: Which criteria reduce apixaban to 2.5 mg BID in atrial fibrillation?

options.t: Any 2 of these 3: age 80 or older, weight 60 kg or less, SCr 1.5 mg/dL or higher
options.why: Eliquis label. One criterion is not enough.
Age alone does not qualify.
The apixaban AF rule uses SCr, age and weight, not CrCl.

steps.q: How many does she meet?

options.t: One: age 82. Weight 64 kg and SCr 1.2 do not qualify
options.why: So the correct dose is 5 mg BID.
Recheck: 64 kg is above 60, and 1.2 is below 1.5.

steps.q: Why does underdosing matter?

options.t: Underdosed apixaban leaves her less protected from stroke without a proven bleeding benefit
options.why: Off label dose reduction is one of the most common DOAC errors.

options.t: It does not matter; lower is always safer
options.why: Stroke is the harm you are preventing.

cases.call: **S/B:** 82 years old, 64 kg, SCr 1.2, AF, apixaban 2.5 mg BID ordered. **A:** She meets only 1 of the 3 dose reduction criteria. **R:** I recommend apixaban 5 mg BID, which the label supports for her.

sources.t: Eliquis (apixaban) prescribing information, Pfizer

workup.calc: Age 82 (meets 1), weight 64 kg (not 60 or less), SCr 1.2 (not 1.5 or more): **1 of 3** so **5 mg BID**.

cases.title: Rivaroxaban and food
cases.stem: New DVT. Order: rivaroxaban 15 mg BID at 0600 and 1800, "may give on empty stomach."

steps.q: What is the problem?

options.t: Rivaroxaban 15 mg and 20 mg tablets must be taken with food; absorption drops a lot when fasting
options.why: With food, absorption of the 15 and 20 mg doses is nearly complete.
Fasting lowers exposure for these strengths.

steps.q: What is the VTE treatment schedule?

options.t: 15 mg BID with food for 21 days, then 20 mg daily with food
options.why: Rivaroxaban label.
10 mg daily is for extended prevention after the treatment phase.

cases.pearl: **Rivaroxaban 15 and 20 mg: always with food. VTE: 15 BID x 21 days, then 20 daily.**

sources.t: Xarelto (rivaroxaban) prescribing information, DailyMed

cases.title: Dabigatran down the tube
cases.stem: A patient on dabigatran 150 mg BID now has an NG tube. The nurse asks to open the capsule.

steps.q: Can the capsule be opened?

options.t: No: opening the capsule raises exposure by about 75%, risking bleeding
options.why: Dabigatran must be swallowed whole.
Not allowed for dabigatran capsules.

steps.q: What do you suggest?

options.t: Switch to an anticoagulant that can go through a tube (for example crushed apixaban or rivaroxaban per label, or a heparin product) after team review
options.why: Check the label for each drug's tube instructions and the patient's kidney function.
Leaves the patient unprotected.

sources.t: Pradaxa (dabigatran) prescribing information (via HemOnc)
Eliquis (apixaban) prescribing information, Pfizer
Xarelto (rivaroxaban) prescribing information, DailyMed

cases.title: Edoxaban and great kidneys
cases.stem: A 45 year old man with AF, CrCl 118 mL/min, is admitted on edoxaban 60 mg daily.

steps.q: What does the label warn about?

options.t: In AF, edoxaban should not be used when CrCl is above 95 mL/min because it was less effective at preventing stroke
options.why: High clearance lowers levels. Suggest another anticoagulant.

options.t: Nothing; higher kidney function is always better
options.why: This is the boxed warning for edoxaban in AF.

cases.pearl: **Edoxaban in AF: not if CrCl above 95.**

sources.t: Savaysa (edoxaban) prescribing information, DailyMed

cases.title: DOAC with a mechanical valve
cases.stem: A patient with a mechanical mitral valve is admitted on apixaban, started by an outside clinic.

steps.q: What is the problem?

options.t: DOACs are not recommended for mechanical heart valves; warfarin is the standard
options.why: A dabigatran trial in mechanical valves showed more clots and more bleeding. The apixaban label says use is not recommended.
This is a serious catch.

steps.q: Which other condition is a classic reason to prefer warfarin over a DOAC?

options.t: High risk antiphospholipid syndrome (especially triple positive)
options.why: DOACs had more clots than warfarin in these patients.

options.t: Simple first DVT after knee surgery
options.why: DOACs are fine there.

cases.pearl: **Mechanical valve or high risk antiphospholipid syndrome: warfarin, not a DOAC.**

sources.t: Eliquis (apixaban) prescribing information, Pfizer

cases.title: Extended VTE treatment
cases.stem: A patient with an unprovoked PE has finished 6 months of apixaban 5 mg BID. No bleeding. The team plans to continue.

steps.q: What does CHEST 2021 suggest for extended treatment?

options.t: Reduced dose apixaban 2.5 mg BID (or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily), with no set stop date and a review at least yearly
options.why: AMPLIFY-EXT: recurrent VTE 1.7% on 2.5 mg vs 8.8% on placebo over 12 months.

options.t: Stop at 6 months for every patient
options.why: Unprovoked VTE has high recurrence risk after stopping.
10 mg BID is only for the first 7 days.

steps.q: When is extended treatment usually NOT recommended?

options.t: VTE provoked by a major transient risk factor such as surgery
options.why: Treat 3 months, then stop.

options.t: Unprovoked VTE with low bleeding risk
options.why: That is the group that benefits.

cases.pearl: **Unprovoked VTE after 6 months: apixaban 2.5 BID or rivaroxaban 10 daily, review yearly.**

sources.t: Stevens SM, et al. Antithrombotic therapy for VTE disease: second update of the CHEST guideline. Chest 2021;160:e545-e608
Eliquis (apixaban) prescribing information, Pfizer

cases.title: Warfarin INR of 7
cases.stem: INR 7.2 on warfarin 5 mg daily. No bleeding. She started TMP SMX 3 days ago.

steps.q: What is the likely cause?

options.t: TMP SMX inhibits warfarin metabolism (CYP2C9) and raises INR
options.why: Antibiotics are the most common cause of a sudden INR rise.
Possible, but the interaction explains it.

steps.q: What is the usual management for INR 4.5 to 10 without bleeding?

options.t: Hold warfarin, recheck INR; routine vitamin K is usually not needed
options.why: Low dose oral vitamin K did not reduce bleeding vs placebo in this range (Crowther 2009).
Too much: causes warfarin resistance when you restart.
Only for major bleeding or urgent surgery.

steps.q: What other warfarin interactions do you watch for?

options.why: Common hospital starts.
Strong inducer.
Not a meaningful single dose interaction.

cases.pearl: **INR 4.5 to 10, no bleed: hold, recheck. Find the cause (often an antibiotic).**

sources.t: Crowther MA, et al. Oral vitamin K vs placebo for excessive anticoagulation. Ann Intern Med 2009;150:293-300

cases.title: Warfarin and a major bleed
cases.stem: GI bleed, hemoglobin dropping, INR 5.4, weight 70 kg, on warfarin for AF.

steps.q: What is the 4F-PCC dose?

options.why: Kcentra label: INR 2 to below 4: 25 units/kg (max 2,500); 4 to 6: 35 units/kg (max 3,500); above 6: 50 units/kg (max 5,000).
That is for INR 2 to below 4.
That is for INR above 6.

steps.q: What must be given with 4F-PCC?

options.why: 4F-PCC wears off; vitamin K lets the liver make its own factors so the INR does not rebound.
Without vitamin K the INR rises again.

steps.q: Which contraindication do you check on Kcentra?

options.t: Known history of heparin induced thrombocytopenia (the product contains heparin)
options.why: Also note the boxed warning for arterial and venous clots.
Not related.

cases.pearl: **Warfarin major bleed: 4F-PCC by INR (25, 35, 50 units/kg; weight capped at 100 kg) + vitamin K 10 mg IV.**

sources.t: Kcentra prescribing information, DailyMed

workup.calc: INR 5.4 is in the 4 to 6 band: 35 units/kg x 70 kg = **2,450 units** (under the 3,500 cap) + vitamin K 10 mg IV.

cases.title: Reversing a DOAC in a brain bleed
cases.stem: Intracerebral hemorrhage. Last apixaban dose 4 hours ago.

steps.q: What is the usual reversal in the US now?

options.t: 4F-PCC (commonly 50 units/kg or a fixed dose per protocol)
options.why: Andexanet alfa was withdrawn from the US market in December 2025, so 4F-PCC is the main option.
Vitamin K does nothing for factor Xa inhibitors.
Protamine reverses heparin, not apixaban.

steps.q: And for dabigatran?

options.why: A specific antibody that binds dabigatran.
Idarucizumab is the specific agent.

steps.q: What BP target does the 2022 ICH guideline suggest when lowering SBP?

options.t: Target about 140 mmHg; avoid dropping below 130
options.why: Too low may harm brain perfusion.
Too aggressive.

cases.pearl: **Xa inhibitor bleed: 4F-PCC. Dabigatran: idarucizumab. Vitamin K only for warfarin.**

sources.t: Greenberg SM, et al. 2022 AHA/ASA guideline for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke 2022;53:e282-e361
Kcentra prescribing information, DailyMed
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose anticoagulation policy and reversal order set (verify locally)

cases.title: Weight based heparin
cases.stem: 90 kg man, new PE, normal kidneys, platelets 240,000. Heparin per protocol.

steps.q: What is the weight based VTE regimen?

options.t: 80 units/kg bolus (7,200 units), then 18 units/kg/h (1,620 units/h)
options.why: Raschke nomogram.
That is the ACS regimen (with caps of 4,000 units and 1,000 units/h).

steps.q: When is the first aPTT or anti Xa drawn?

options.t: 6 hours after the bolus and 6 hours after each rate change
options.why: Heparin reaches a new steady state in about 6 hours.
Too early.

steps.q: What do you check before verifying the bolus?

options.t: Recent enoxaparin or DOAC doses on the MAR
options.why: Overlapping anticoagulants cause bleeding. Many protocols skip the bolus after recent enoxaparin.
Needed to detect HIT and bleeding later.

cases.pearl: **VTE heparin: 80 bolus, 18 per hour. ACS: 60 (max 4,000), 12 (max 1,000). Levels at 6 hours.**

sources.t: Raschke RA, et al. Weight based heparin dosing nomogram. Ann Intern Med 1993;119:874-881
Heparin Sodium Injection prescribing information (DailyMed)
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose anticoagulation policy and reversal order set (verify locally)

workup.calc: 80 units/kg x 90 kg = **7,200 units** bolus; 18 units/kg/h x 90 = **1,620 units/h**. With 25,000 units in 250 mL (100 units/mL, check bag ⚠️): 16.2 mL/h.

cases.title: Suspected HIT
cases.stem: Day 7 of heparin. Platelets fell from 260,000 to 110,000. New swollen left leg.

steps.q: How do you estimate the chance of HIT?

options.t: The 4Ts score: thrombocytopenia (a fall of more than 50%), timing (day 5 to 10), thrombosis, other causes
options.why: This patient scores intermediate to high: a 58% fall, day 7, a new clot.
HIT is about the size of the drop, not a cutoff.

steps.q: What do you recommend now, before test results?

options.t: Stop ALL heparin, including flushes and heparin coated catheters
Start a non heparin anticoagulant such as argatroban (2 mcg/kg/min; 0.5 mcg/kg/min in hepatic impairment)
options.why: HIT causes clots; stopping heparin alone is not enough.
Enoxaparin cross reacts with HIT antibodies.
Not routinely; may worsen clotting.

steps.q: When can warfarin start?

options.t: Only after platelets recover (usually 150,000 or more), overlapping with a non heparin agent for at least 5 days
options.why: Warfarin alone in acute HIT can cause venous limb gangrene.
Too early.

cases.pearl: **HIT: 4Ts. Stop all heparin. Start argatroban (or another non heparin agent). No warfarin until platelets recover.**

sources.t: Cuker A, et al. ASH 2018 guidelines: heparin induced thrombocytopenia. Blood Adv 2018;2:3360-3392
Argatroban Injection prescribing information (2019)

workup.calc: Platelets 260,000 to 110,000 = **58% fall**, day 7, new DVT: 4Ts intermediate to high. Argatroban 2 mcg/kg/min (no hepatic impairment).

cases.title: Enoxaparin and kidneys
cases.stem: 75 kg woman, DVT, CrCl 24 mL/min. Order: enoxaparin 75 mg SC every 12 hours.

steps.q: What is the label dose when CrCl is below 30?

options.t: 1 mg/kg SC once daily (75 mg every 24 hours)
options.why: Enoxaparin builds up in kidney failure.
Twice daily dosing accumulates.

steps.q: What about prophylaxis with CrCl below 30?

options.why: Lovenox label.
Too much.

steps.q: When would you check an anti Xa level?

options.t: Kidney impairment, pregnancy, extremes of weight; peak about 4 hours after the dose, at steady state (around the third or fourth dose)
options.why: Not routine for most patients.
Useful in special populations.

cases.pearl: **Enoxaparin CrCl below 30: treatment 1 mg/kg daily, prophylaxis 30 mg daily.**

sources.t: Lovenox (enoxaparin) prescribing information, Sanofi (2025)

workup.calc: CrCl 24: 1 mg/kg x 75 kg = **75 mg every 24 hours** (not every 12).

cases.title: Stopping a DOAC before surgery
cases.stem: Apixaban 5 mg BID for AF, CrCl 70 mL/min. Elective hip replacement (high bleed risk) on Friday.

steps.q: By the PAUSE schedule, when is the last dose?

options.t: Tuesday is the last day of dosing: skip the 2 days before (Wednesday and Thursday) and the day of surgery
options.why: High bleed risk: about 60 to 68 hours off before surgery.
Too close for high bleed risk.

steps.q: Should she get bridging with enoxaparin?

options.why: PAUSE and CHEST 2022: no bridging for DOACs.
Bridging adds bleeding without benefit.

steps.q: When does apixaban usually restart after high bleed risk surgery?

options.t: About 48 to 72 hours after, once bleeding is controlled
options.why: Prophylactic doses may be used before that per the surgical team.
Too early.

cases.pearl: **PAUSE: high bleed risk, skip 2 days before and the day of. No bridging for DOACs.**

sources.t: Douketis JD, et al. PAUSE. JAMA Intern Med 2019;179:1469-1478
Douketis JD, et al. Perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy: CHEST guideline. Chest 2022;162:e207-e243

workup.calc: Surgery Friday, high bleed risk: no apixaban Wednesday or Thursday or Friday morning; Tuesday is the last dosing day (about 60 to 68 hours off).

cases.title: Bridging warfarin
cases.stem: Warfarin for AF (CHA2DS2-VASc 3), stopping for a procedure. The team orders enoxaparin bridging.

steps.q: What does the evidence say?

options.t: CHEST 2022 recommends against bridging in AF; BRIDGE showed no difference in clots and more major bleeding with bridging (3.2% vs 1.3%)
options.why: Strong recommendation against bridging in AF.
That was old practice.

steps.q: Who may still be bridged?

options.t: Very high risk patients, for example a mechanical mitral valve or a clot in the last 3 months, per cardiology or hematology
options.why: Individual decision; check St. Mary's policy.
Some very high risk patients are bridged.

cases.pearl: **AF on warfarin: do not bridge. Stop about 5 days before.**

sources.t: Douketis JD, et al. Perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy: CHEST guideline. Chest 2022;162:e207-e243
Douketis JD, et al. Perioperative bridging in AF (BRIDGE). N Engl J Med 2015;373:823-833

cases.title: The duplicate anticoagulant
cases.stem: A patient transferred from the ICU has heparin infusion running, apixaban 5 mg BID newly ordered, and heparin 5,000 units SC every 8 hours still active.

steps.q: What do you find?

options.why: Transfers are where duplicates happen.
Major bleeding risk.

steps.q: How should a heparin infusion transition to apixaban?

options.t: Start apixaban when the heparin infusion is stopped (within about the same time), and discontinue the SC heparin
options.why: Per labels, switch at the time the infusion stops.
Unsafe.

cases.pearl: **On every transfer: count the anticoagulants. One at a time.**

sources.t: Eliquis (apixaban) prescribing information, Pfizer
St. Mary's pharmacy to dose anticoagulation policy and reversal order set (verify locally)

cases.title: Shift simulation: anticoagulation calls
cases.stem: Three calls: (1) aPTT came back very high on a heparin drip, patient now has blood in the urine; (2) a question about whether apixaban can be crushed; (3) an INR of 3.4 (goal 2 to 3) on a stable patient.

steps.q: Which first?

options.t: The heparin patient who is bleeding with a high aPTT
options.why: Active bleeding on a drug that can be stopped right now.
Can wait.
Mildly high, stable.

steps.q: What do you advise for the bleeding heparin patient?

options.t: Hold the infusion per protocol, notify the prescriber, check hemoglobin; consider protamine if bleeding is serious (1 mg per 100 units given in the last 2 to 3 hours, max 50 mg)
options.why: Heparin half life is short, so stopping often works quickly.
Wrong direction.

steps.q: Can apixaban be crushed?

options.t: Yes: tablets may be crushed and given in water, D5W or apple juice, or through an NG tube, per label
options.why: Unlike dabigatran.
Apixaban can be crushed.

cases.pearl: **Bleeding on a drip first. Protamine 1 mg per 100 units (max 50 mg).**
